body:
WHAT
WebSearch returns titles, URLs and snippets for a query. The backend comes from settings.search.provider: DuckDuckGo (default, no key, scrapes the HTML endpoint via parseDuckDuckGoHtml), Brave or Tavily (each needs an API key read from the env var named in settings.search.apiKeyEnv). All three produce the same SearchResult shape. allowed_domains keeps only matching hosts (including subdomains); blocked_domains drops them. search.enabled:false returns an error telling the agent not to retry.

WHY
Without a normalized result shape the agent's output would differ per provider, and without domain filters it could not restrict itself to trusted sources.

WHERE
engine/tools/src/webSearch.ts — SearchResult/SearchBackend interfaces, parseDuckDuckGoHtml() (exported; uses resolveDdgUrl() to decode uddg redirect links and drop y.js ads, stripHtml()), class DuckDuckGoBackend, class BraveBackend (maps web.results description->snippet), class TavilyBackend (maps results content->snippet), webSearchTool.execute() (provider switch, apiKeyEnv checks, filterByDomain()), hostOf(), domainMatches().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. parseDuckDuckGoHtml on a fixture with two result__a anchors (one uddg-encoded link, one y.js ad) and result__snippet anchors returns one SearchResult with the decoded URL, entity-decoded title and snippet, and the ad excluded.
2. Stub fetch to return a Brave JSON { web: { results: [{title,url,description}] } } and a Tavily JSON { results: [{title,url,content}] }; assert BraveBackend and TavilyBackend both return [{ title, url, snippet }] with snippet taken from description/content respectively.
3. With a fake backend returning hosts docs.example.com, example.com and other.org, execute with allowed_domains ['example.com']; assert only the first two remain; with blocked_domains ['example.com'] only other.org remains.
4. With settings.search { provider:'brave' } and no apiKeyEnv, assert isError and the message asks to set search.apiKeyEnv; with apiKeyEnv 'X_KEY' unset in process.env assert the message names X_KEY; with enabled:false assert the 'disabled in settings' error.
5. A backend that throws yields isError 'Search failed: ...'; a backend returning [] yields 'No results for "<query>".' without isError; results are rendered numbered '1. title\n url\n snippet'.
